source_review.notes: Reviewed the primary Driscoll-Sarnak-Sleator-Tarjan paper, the primary Sarnak-Tarjan persistent-search-tree report and its Princeton record, MIT 6.854 and 6.851 graduate notes, the 2021 MIT 6.851 lecture record, and Aarhus University's Brodal publication record. All seven final cited destinations returned HTTP 200.

evidence: Checked ephemeral states, linear version domain/latest, logical and physical nodes, fields, birth versions, histories, history length, versioned values, roots, primitive-step count, bounded in-degree, slot capacity, skew, and rebasing.
Checked partial persistence, physical append mutation, functional immutability, rollback, full persistence, and confluent persistence remain distinct.
notation_and_syntax.notes: The chapter consistently uses numeric predecessor selection only for a linear partial-persistence history.

evidence: Recomputed the four executable list versions, the rejected-old-update result, and every expected invariant/output line.
Recomputed the example predecessor values P,Q,Q,R,R,S,S and the 1,024-record binary-search depth of about ten comparison levels.
Recomputed the rebasing example: predecessor at version 100 is C, so C becomes the surviving base before record (150,D).
numerical_recomputation.notes: Numerical examples are finite illustrations and are not measurements of the transformation's asymptotic overhead.

evidence: Verified the fat-node induction: exact changed records simulate the new ephemeral state and later stamps cannot affect an earlier predecessor query.
Verified a traversal's cost is the sum of per-field predecessor lookups and that O(log h) sharpens the coarser O(log m) statement.

Reviewed the node-copying potential proof shape and confirmed the chapter conditions every constant-overhead claim on primitive pointer-machine steps, bounded in-degree, fixed node fields, sufficient slots, exact predecessors, and the published construction.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: No invented modification-slot constant or generalized RAM/concurrency theorem is asserted.

evidence: Reviewed version zero/latest/future/expired/foreign/stale handles, duplicate stamps, same-field multiwrite, no-op/null pointer, node births, root and multi-root changes, and rejected old-version updates.
Reviewed empty and hot histories, mixed-version traversal, unbounded in-degree, full-slot cascades, incomplete copies, missing predecessor/root redirects, parent/back pointers, and external handles.
Reviewed publication failure/crash, writer conflicts, moving history arrays, reader pins, rebase, ID reuse, malformed/cyclic imports, quotas, checksums, and recovery.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Adversarial resource controls cover nodes, records, bytes, history length, versions, roots, traversal depth/steps, pins, imports, staging, and diagnostics.

evidence: The executable checks strictly ordered per-field histories, birth constraints, all four independent expected sequences, historical noninterference after rejection, and latest-only enforcement.
The chapter specifies history, graph, copying, transaction, lifetime, concurrency, serialization, recovery, and structure-specific invariants.
The evidence plan compares all retained versions with independent snapshots and adds property, metamorphic, fault, parser, reclamation, and copy-cascade tests.
invariant_checking.notes: The executable intentionally omits node copying, multi-field transactions, persistence to disk, reclamation, and concurrency.

evidence: Reviewed the abstract latest-only contract, per-field predecessor semantics, root/birth handling, simulation induction, and atomic logical-version publication.
Reviewed bounded-slot copying, predecessor redirection, root propagation, bounded-degree theorem boundary, and amortized potential shape against the primary paper and MIT notes.
Reviewed version consistency, handles, transactional failure, reader/writer memory safety, retention/rebase, serialization/import, recovery, security, tests, and benchmarks.
proof_review.notes: Brodal's worst-case result is labeled as a distinct later construction rather than attributed to basic node copying.

evidence: The simulation proof names complete instrumentation, linear order, latest-only updates, version-consistent reads, births, coalescing, publication, and lifetime assumptions.
The amortized argument is explicitly a proof shape and directs implementers to the exact construction for slot constants and postprocessing.
The chapter separates proven model results from implementation obligations, operational measurements, and the finite Python demonstration.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: No claim that fat nodes, node copying, or partial persistence is universally optimal appears.

evidence: The standard-library Python trace passed exact twelve-line stdout, empty stderr, and zero exit status under the locally recorded Python toolchain.
It emits evidence=finite_fat_node_partial_history and reproduces four historical sequences, update rejection, noninterference, ordered histories, birth constraints, and version consistency.
All seven external citation destinations returned HTTP 200 and all repository-local links passed module validation.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No copying cascade, transaction failure, storage, recovery, reclamation, concurrency, parser hostility, or production performance was empirically evaluated.

conceptual_review.notes: The chapter progresses from the latest-only semantic contract through unlimited histories and simulation, bounded-slot copying and theorem assumptions, then publication, concurrency, retention, serialization, security, and evidence.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed scoped version handles, explicit views, field/root completeness, transaction coalescing, atomic/durable publication, pointer-machine fit, reverse pointers, copy cascades, reader pinning, writer conflict, rebase, stable IDs, quarantine imports, quotas, checksums, recovery, fault testing, and workload-shaped metrics.

pedagogical_review.notes: Starts from first principles, derives predecessor semantics and simulation, distinguishes theorem units and assumptions, includes ten varied examples and one reproducible history trace, then provides five progressive exercises with complete model answers.

limitations: Internal authoring, primary/official-source, mathematical, executable-snippet, conceptual, practitioner, and pedagogical evidence only; no external academic, Driscoll/Sarnak/Sleator/Tarjan, Brodal, MIT, Princeton, persistence, security, reliability, storage, performance, or independent practitioner review is claimed. The chapter and finite list trace prove neither arbitrary fat-node/copying implementations, node-copying slot constants, worst-case basic-copy update time, unbounded-degree transformation bounds, arbitrary RAM/array/hash representations, multi-field atomicity, full/confluent/functional persistence, isolation/MVCC, memory-model safety, linearizability/progress, reclamation/rebasing, crash consistency/recovery, hostile-import security, production cache/memory/tail behavior, certification, nor deployment fitness.
